title: What Changes When You Hit $100,000 Net Worth
description:
Charlie Munger said the first $100,000 is the hardest. So what actually changes when your net worth finally hits $100,000? In this video I go through 15 changes, with real math on compounding, fees and time, plus how long it really takes to get there.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:19 How we got the numbers
1:46 The big picture
3:27 1. Compounding becomes visible
4:40 2. Your money out-earns your savings
5:29 3. The rule of 72 gets real
6:24 4. You think in net worth
7:18 5. Fees start to hurt
8:54 6. Allocation beats stock picking
9:44 7. Drops feel real
11:03 8. Taxes matter more
12:01 9. You need a real emergency fund
13:18 10. Home equity isn't cash
14:20 11. High-interest debt is an emergency
15:09 12. You become a sales target
16:05 13. Paperwork matters
16:52 14. Your options multiply
17:39 15. The trap
19:05 $100,000 at 25, 40 and 55
21:58 How long it takes to reach $100,000
23:05 Three paths to $100,000
24:56 What to do this week
25:54 Five mistakes on the way
26:40 Questions people ask
30:43 Recap: all 15 changes
31:27 What to do next

Sources:
- Federal Reserve, Survey of Consumer Finances 2022 (median net worth $192,700; by age: under 35 $39,040, 35-44 $135,300)
- Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2025 (20% experienced fraud or scams)
- IRS, retirement plan and IRA rules (check current limits)
- Rule of 72 and compound growth: stated illustrative math at 7% average yearly return

Photos: Wikimedia Commons contributors. Full credits and licenses: https://github.com/ryan-rover-money-channel/ryan-rover-money/blob/main/agendamento/creditos/video02.md

This video is for education only and is not financial advice. Numbers are illustrations, not promises.
